action: Customers: watch for notices from The Container Store; the article gives no company instruction. Retailers: keep an offline fallback for payment processing.
date_note: The Record (20 Nov) quotes the company saying the incident was 'this past weekend'; no exact day is given, so the article date is used.
exec: A US retailer had to stop online ordering and run limited in-store payments after a cyberattack, showing how quickly an incident can disrupt sales.
plain: The Container Store says it has restored its website and systems after a cybersecurity incident last weekend. Online ordering was shut down and stores used alternative ways to process transactions.
summary: The Record reports that parent company Neighborhood Intelligence said The Container Store restored its website and systems after a cybersecurity incident this past weekend. The incident forced online ordering offline and limited in-store transaction processing, and the company hired cybersecurity experts. The article says the group n0n listed the retailer on its leak site; the company did not address that claim.
title: Container Store restores systems after cyberattack

validation.note: One outlet (The Record, 20 Nov) read in full; it quotes the company statement. The company's own statement was not read.

review.note: Compared restoration, online ordering shutdown, limited in-store processing, experts hired, n0n leak-site claim unaddressed and 20 Nov date against The Record
